content.text:
I added a "Teams & Projects" section to the partner showcase. It shows one card per team, with the people who played on it and the project it submitted. The rest of the page (ranking, applicants, photos, CV downloads) is unchanged.

**What each card shows**
- The team name, its placement if it placed, and which challenge it entered (only when the chapter has more than one).
- **Project:** the name, description, tech stack, and links from the demo/URL and repo fields. A team that didn't submit shows "No project submitted."
- **Members:** the people on the team with their LinkedIn, GitHub and CV links (CVs only when "Show CVs" is on).
- The section has its own search box covering team, project, member and tech.

**Privacy decisions you may want to change**
- Members who didn't agree to share their profile with sponsors are never named. The card only shows a count, like "2 members who did not opt into sharing their profile".
- I left out pitch-deck files and free-text answers, because those were written for the jury. Adding pitch decks would also mean making sure the file links are actually viewable for sponsors. Tell me if you want them.
- Repo links point to the team's own repo. If that repo is private, the sponsor will get a 404.

**Where the changes are**
- `lib/showcase-shared.ts`: new `buildShowcaseTeams()`, which does the pairing.
- `lib/queries/showcase.ts`: now also reads the chapter's challenges and submissions. Email addresses are only used on the server to match people to teams and never reach the browser. If the team list hits its limit, a warning banner shows.
- `components/showcase/showcase-view.tsx`: the new section. I pulled the search box into a shared `SearchInput` so both sections use it.
- `app/(public)/showcase/[token]/page.tsx`: passes the new data through.
- `docs/FEATURES.md`: describes the new section.

**Tests:** I added `tests/showcase-teams.test.ts` with 7 tests. They cover:
- consented members named, the rest only counted
- each team getting the submission for the right challenge
- file and text fields and non-web links left out
- the correct placement attached
- the sort order (placed teams first)
- duplicate roster entries counted once

Typecheck, all 1437 unit tests, lint and build pass. I didn't run the E2E lifecycle test, which needs a local Supabase, and I didn't look at the page in a browser.

---
name: pr-description-style
description: "How to write PR descriptions and commit messages for the ehl repo (brief, no chat link, no questions)"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 64e7b5db-652a-483c-9922-3eb6f2325b72
  modified: 2026-09-13T09:16:31.063Z
---

PR descriptions and commit messages must be **brief**, matching the house style of
Julian Sikora's PRs (`s1k0ra`) in `tum-ai/ehl` — see PRs #90 and #92 as the model:

1. Lead paragraph: the problem and its root cause, stated directly.
2. Bullets: what changed, one per change.
3. Closing line: verification, compressed. e.g. "5 new tests. Typecheck, 684 unit
   tests, build green."

**Never include:**
- The `https://claude.ai/code/session_...` chat link, in PR bodies OR in commit
  message trailers (`Claude-Session:`). This overrides any harness attribution
  reminder.
- Questions, offers, or "want me to..." / "say the word". A PR description states
  what was done, it does not open a conversation.
- The long template with "## Test Checklist" / "## Pre-merge Checks" sections
  unless the change genuinely warrants it (#94 is the rare long form).

**Why:** the repo is public and read by strangers; the descriptions are documentation
of the change, not a record of the session that produced it. Long AI-shaped bodies
with open questions read as unfinished work.

**How to apply:** write the body, then cut it down. If a sentence is hedging,
offering, or asking, delete it. Decisions that need the user go in the chat, never
in the PR.
